package_info.package_manager: N/A (injected JavaScript, typically in web assets)
package_info.why_malicious: The package injects obfuscated JavaScript code that impersonates Google Tag Manager, using encoded strings to hide a malicious URL and exfiltrate sensitive data (e.g., credit card information) from compromised web pages.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the web page loads and the script executes in the browser)
execution_context.file_location: Injected <script> tag in HTML (impersonating Google Tag Manager)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code creates a script element with its source set to a base64-decoded string (obfuscated malicious URL), then injects it into the DOM, causing the browser to load and execute additional malicious JavaScript from the hidden URL.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code uses obfuscated (base64-encoded) strings to hide the true destination of a dynamically injected script, and leverages eval-like dynamic execution patterns to load further code from an external, hidden source.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate analytics or tag manager scripts do not obfuscate their URLs or dynamically inject scripts from encoded sources. They use transparent, well-known URLs and static script tags.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate scripts may use dynamic script injection for feature loading, but they do not obfuscate URLs or use encoded strings to hide destinations.
key_indicators: Base64-encoded string used as a script source
Dynamic script injection into the DOM
Obfuscated code structure and variable names

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated JavaScript is injected into the web page, impersonating Google Tag Manager.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the obfuscated code in the browser.

attack_chain.action: At runtime, the code decodes a base64-encoded string to reveal a malicious URL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Dynamic creation and injection of a script element with the malicious URL as its source.

attack_chain.action: The browser loads and executes additional malicious JavaScript from the hidden URL, enabling data exfiltration (e.g., credit card skimming).
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: Dynamic script injection using obfuscated or encoded URLs
Base64 or other encoded strings decoded at runtime to produce network destinations
Impersonation of legitimate analytics or tag manager scripts with hidden destinations
High-entropy string blocks in JavaScript code
file_indicators: Presence of base64-encoded strings in inline or external JavaScript
Unusual script tags claiming to be Google Tag Manager but with non-standard URLs
network_indicators: Outbound requests to domains revealed only after decoding obfuscated strings
Unexpected script loads from non-standard or suspicious domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan JavaScript code for high-entropy strings and common encoding patterns (base64, RC4, XOR, etc.), especially those used as arguments to dynamic script injection functions. Flag scripts that decode and inject URLs at runtime, particularly if they claim to be from well-known services (e.g., Google Tag Manager) but use non-standard or hidden destinations. Monitor for outbound network requests to domains not present in the original source code but revealed only after decoding.
